Question ID: GEO_U05_L03_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.6

In cyclic quadrilateral 1, one angle measures 70°. What is the measure of its opposite angle?

feedback.text: This treats opposite angles as congruent, but cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles are supplementary.
Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary, so 180° - 70° = 110°.
This adds without using the 180° supplementary relationship.
The opposite angle can be determined because cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles are supplementary.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L03_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.6

Triangle 2 is inscribed in a circle with one side as a diameter. If one acute angle is 28°, what is the other acute angle?

feedback.text: The acute angles are not necessarily congruent.
This ignores the triangle angle sum and the right angle from the diameter.
The angle opposite the diameter is 90°, not the remaining acute angle.
An angle that intercepts a diameter is 90°, so the two acute angles sum to 90°.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L03_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.6

An inscribed triangle has an angle intercepting an arc of 100°. What is that angle measure?

feedback.text: An inscribed angle measures half its intercepted arc.
This would match a central angle, not an inscribed angle.
This doubles the arc instead of halving it.
The intercepted arc is given, so the inscribed angle can be determined.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L03_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.6

Quadrilateral 4 is inscribed in a circle. Which pair of opposite angle measures could be valid?

feedback.text: Equal opposite angles are not required; they must be supplementary.
These values do not show the required 180° sum for opposite angles.
Opposite angles in an inscribed quadrilateral must have a sum of 180°.
These angles sum to 135°, not 180°.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L03_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.6

In the described circle situation, two inscribed angles intercept the same arc. What can be concluded?

feedback.text: Same intercepted arc supports congruence, not necessarily supplementary angles.

answer.text: The two inscribed angles are congruent.

feedback.text: Inscribed angles intercepting the same arc have equal measures.

answer.text: Each angle equals the full arc measure.

feedback.text: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.
The shared intercepted arc gives enough evidence for a conclusion.
